Subject: Tuesday reading club — update before the review on 18 November

Dear Niamh,

I wanted to send you an update on the Tuesday reading club at Knocknacarra library before the review meeting on Wednesday 18 November. There is some lovely news to share, and there is also something I need to put right with you.

Since your email of 30 October about pausing the club from January, attendance has reached 14 children — that was our number last Tuesday, 3 November. We had five most weeks in September and were up to nine by mid-October, so it feels as though the club is finally finding its feet. I came home last Tuesday absolutely delighted.

We have been meeting in the upstairs meeting room on Tuesdays, from 3.30 to 4.45, since September 2025, and it has taken time to build. Now, though, there is a real pleasure in the room. Two sisters from a Ukrainian family joined us in October, and the older girl now reads to her younger sister in English at the end of each session. Another child, who would scarcely open a book in September, asked last week whether he could take two home. As a former teacher, you can imagine how much that meant to me.

We have also had a very generous donation from Declan Moran, who owns Salthill Book Nook: 120 books, mostly for the six-to-nine age group, with a good few as Gaeilge. It gives us much more choice for the children as their interests and confidence grow.

I do understand that your email raised both low attendance and the increase in hall insurance, and that better numbers do not make the insurance difficulty disappear. Still, I would be grateful if you could bring these new figures to the review and reconsider the January pause. It would be a terrible pity to stop just as things seem to be taking off.

The other matter is the Corrib Courier. I met Orla Keane, their reporter, at the farmers’ market and got carried away telling her about the club. I said, “Come along any Tuesday,” without checking with you first. She would now like to come on Tuesday 24 November with a photographer.

I was wrong not to check first, plain and simple, and I wanted you to hear it directly from me. I know that photographs of the children require your sign-off and the parental consent forms. My invitation should not have been made before speaking to you, and I do not want it to put you under any pressure to agree.

I am happy to ring Orla and put the visit on hold until you have decided whether it should go ahead. If you do approve it, I would also be glad to collect the consent forms myself, following your guidance. The coverage could be wonderful for the club, but only if it is done properly.

Thank you for considering all of this, Niamh, and for the work you put into keeping the volunteer programme going. I hope the new numbers give us something encouraging to work with before the 18th.

Warm wishes,

[Your name]
